items.heading: Jessie Buckley wins Best Actress at the Oscars
items.body: On 15 March Jessie Buckley won the Oscar for Best Actress for Hamnet. The Irish Times called her Ireland's first ever best actress winner. Brenda Fricker won in 1990, but that was the supporting category, so this is a fresh first. Richard Baneham also collected a third Oscar that night, for visual effects. A very good night for Irish film.

items.heading: Rory McIlroy wins the Masters again
items.body: Rory McIlroy, from Holywood in Co. Down, kept the Green Jacket. On Sunday 12 April he won the Masters for the second year in a row, finishing twelve under par after a closing round of 71 and beating Scottie Scheffler by one shot. It is his sixth major. The same month, Dermot Kennedy's album The Weight of the Woods landed at number one in Ireland, his third in a row.

pages.heading: Sport
pages.body: Big days at Croke Park, a big year for women's sport and a few firsts. We also remember Ciara Mageean, our European 1500m champion, who died on 1 November, aged 34.
pages.note: Mageean mention is in the divider body only. A full tribute page is for the tribute writer.

pages.heading: Katie Taylor says goodbye at Croke Park
pages.body: Around 80,000 people filled Croke Park for Katie Taylor's last fight. She beat Flora Pili of France by unanimous decision, with two judges scoring it one hundred points to ninety. Asked for something inspiring afterwards, she said "Let me just look around." She retired as a three time undisputed world champion. What a way to finish.

items.title: Athletics Ireland hits a record
items.blurb: Athletics Ireland reaches an all time high of 76,507 registered members.

pages.heading: Records and firsts: everyday Ireland
bullets: Jessie Buckley became the first Irish woman to win the Best Actress Oscar, on 15 March.
Summer was provisionally the hottest on record, at 16.28 degrees. The old record was 16.19, set in 2025.
July was Dublin Airport's busiest month ever, with 3,839,635 passengers.
Wind power hit a record 3,898 megawatts on 14 February. Solar passed one gigawatt for the first time on 20 April.
A record 70,411 students got their Leaving Cert results in August.
Irish agri-food exports reached a record 20.8 billion euro for 2025.

pages.heading: Top 10 big moments for the country
pages.body: Chosen by UBP from published coverage. Good news only. Not an official ranking.

items.title: Jessie Buckley wins an Oscar
items.blurb: Jessie Buckley becomes the first Irish winner of the Best Actress Oscar for Hamnet.

items.title: Katie Taylor's farewell
items.blurb: Katie Taylor retires as a three time undisputed world champion at Croke Park.

items.title: Mayo end the wait
items.blurb: Mayo win their fourth All-Ireland football title, the first since 1951.

items.title: Solar power surges
items.blurb: Grid solar tops 1 gigawatt in April. Installed solar passes 3 gigawatts by August.

items.title: A record crowd for camogie
items.blurb: A record 33,419 fans watch the camogie final at Croke Park.

items.title: A record Leaving Cert year
items.blurb: Leaving Cert participation hits a record 70,411, the highest in the exam's 100 year history.

items.title: U2 are back at number one
items.blurb: U2 score their eleventh Irish number one album with Carnaval De Luz.

items.title: First graduates of an inclusive programme
items.blurb: Twelve students become the first graduates of TU Dublin's Independent Living Skills programme.

items.title: Student fee cut
items.blurb: Budget 2027 cuts the student contribution by 150 euro, to 2,350 euro.

items.title: Apprenticeships keep growing
items.blurb: Ireland now has 30,536 apprentices working with 10,191 companies.
